title: Simple uptime checks and alerts
when: A small site or API needs to tell someone when it goes down, without running a full monitoring stack.
prompt:
Goal: An outside checker that polls each health URL, alerts after repeated failures, announces recovery and keeps a short history.
Steps:
1. Run it from another machine or network than the service, so an outage cannot silence it.
2. check.sh per URL: curl -fsS --max-time 10 -o body.tmp -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}" "$URL"; for the home page also grep body.tmp for an expected word.
3. A state file per URL keeps the consecutive failure count and last status.
4. Alert on the second failure in a row, once per outage; on recovery send the downtime length.
5. Deliver via the local mail command or an HTTP POST to a chat webhook whose URL comes from an env file.
6. Daily extras: certificate days left, disk over 80 percent, newest backup older than 26 hours.
7. Append each result to checks.log as one ISO timestamped line; a weekly summary prints uptime percent.
8. Schedule every minute under flock -n.
Quality bar:
- One outage gives one alert and one recovery message.
- A timeout counts as a failure.
- Adding a URL is one line in urls.txt.
Pitfalls:
- Checking from the server that goes down with the app.
- Alerting on every failed run until people mute the channel.
- A health URL that answers 200 while the app is broken.
Verify:
- [ ] Every request has a timeout.
- [ ] Failure threshold and recovery message present.
- [ ] Webhook URL read from the environment.
- [ ] A lock prevents overlapping runs.
Output: monitor/check.sh, monitor/urls.txt and a Monitoring section in the ops notes.

examples.input: me avise quando meu site cair
examples.output: monitor/check.sh run every minute with flock, curl --max-time 10, alert on 2 failures, recovery message, checks.log history
